title: RLC-NR: work out a better id/data value for adding fragments.
description:
Record frame number with starting segment for each SN.
This allows reassembly to work if there is a reset, or even
the same PDU retransmitted and re-segmented with different
MAC grant sizes.

notes.body:
How does this work if after a reset you receive the second fragment of a given SN before the first one? Will not this second fragment used with the previous instance (and now invalid) of this SN?
IMHO it would be better to create a new reassembly table after a RLC reset, or to keep a counter that is locally incremented each time a reset occurs and that is systematically added to the tree key. Something similar to the open_count in packet-mbim.c for example.

Hi Pascal,

I had meant to clear out the entry for reassembly_start_table once re-assembly was complete, then *maybe* I could relax the check at line 613 for only starting new entries on the starting segment?

I was reluctant to try to count the resets indicated by RRC as they are not always visible in logs I look at (depending on how they're captured), i.e.  for NSA I sometimes might not see the LTE RRC frames.  Another complication is that if AM ACKs are not forthcoming, you might see the same SN resent with a different segmentation without a reset happening.

Often the logs I'm looking at will not show MAC TB retransmissions (which could effectively change the order segments are seen).  I suppose the harqid should arguably be added to the key.  And currently I'm not seeing MIMO where segments are really in-order, but logging order might not match the segment offset (i.e. so starting segment might not be seen first).

I could try to use timing information as a clue, but worry that it'll end up in fuzzy/confusing logic.

Would you object to me clearing out the entry once reassembly is complete, but otherwise merging as-is (with some comments pointing out its shortcomings) ?
I'm not a user of this functionality so feel free to merge it as is if you want. I don't think it can work properly though.
